title: introduce-retry-advice-schema-and-fail-fast-mode-for-tool-calls
author: Marina Lopez
release_notes: Adds a machine-readable Retry-Advice header and an opt-in fail-fast surface for streamed tool/function calls. Improves error-code normalization and documents idempotency scoping for multiplexed tool sessions.
description:
Context and motivation:
We have inconsistent retry signals across the API surface when tool/function calls are streamed or multiplexed. Clients cannot reliably determine whether they should back off, fast-fail, or retry idempotently when a partial tool result is observed. This causes duplicated side-effects for third-party tools and poor UX during transient capacity or regional failovers.

Goals:
- Provide a compact, machine-readable Retry-Advice schema surface in responses and handshake frames so clients can make deterministic decisions without parsing freeform Retry-After text.
- Add an opt-in fail-fast mode for tool/function calls so latency-sensitive consumers can choose early termination when capacity is constrained.
- Clarify idempotency scoping for tool-session keys (session-scoped vs call-scoped) and document expected semantics for retries during multiplexed streams.
- Normalize error codes and a short error-class header so compatibility layers (OpenAI shim) map to consistent programmatic values.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Introduces a Retry-Advice header (Retry-Advice: token=<opaque>, retry_ms=<int>, scope=<call|session>, reason=<enum>) that can be returned on regular HTTP responses and as a control frame on streaming channels. The header is intentionally small and parseable without full JSON decoding.
- Adds a small handshake frame in the streaming protocol (control.advice) that mirrors the Retry-Advice header for in-band retries during long-running tool calls.
- Adds an opt-in fail-fast flag (X-Redwood-FailFast: true) at request level and a server-side backpressure path that returns 409+Retry-Advice when capacity is insufficient. Fail-fast is opt-in to avoid changing default behaviors.
- Documents idempotency scoping: idempotency-key: session:<uuid> and idempotency-key: call:<uuid>. Server treats session-scoped keys as safe to retry for non-destructive operations across stream reconnects; call-scoped keys are single-attempt-only by default.
- Normalizes structured error codes into X-Redwood-Err and a small textual code in the JSON body (error.code_short) to make OpenAI-compat layer mapping simple and deterministic.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime: change concentrated in rpc/streaming/control.go and rpc/http/headers.go. Added a lightweight parsing helper for Retry-Advice that avoids allocations on the hot path.
- OpenAI shim: map new X-Redwood-Err and Retry-Advice into OpenAI-friendly counterparts (x-openai-retry and retry_after_ms) in redwood-openai-compat adapter.
- SDKs: hooks implemented in redwood-sdk-python to expose a parsed RetryAdvice object and an experimental Client.fail_fast option. Typescript/Go SDKs receive follow-up patches to maintain small diffs.
- Tests: unit and integration tests added for backpressure, fail-fast, and idempotency-scope semantics; added a synthetic load test in perf-canary to validate behavior under constrained GPU pools.

Checklist:
- [x] Design and spec in Linear ENG-4321
- [x] Runtime parsing and control frame implementation
- [x] OpenAI-adapter mapping
- [x] SDK Python exposure and docs
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Observability: metrics for advice_emitted and advice_consumed
- [x] Rollout plan and feature gating behind feature flag (feature.retry_advice_v1)

Compatibility and rollout:
- This is backward-compatible by default: servers will only emit Retry-Advice when advantage is present; clients will ignore unknown headers. Fail-fast is opt-in. The OpenAI shim will translate fields to legacy retry_after semantics when clients expect them.
- Rollout plan: feature flag default off for 2 weeks in staging, controlled activation for select tenants, then global enable. We added metrics and tracing spans to detect any increase in client-side retries or side-effect duplication.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: header parsing, handshake encoding/decoding, idempotency-scope transitions.
- Integration: simulated reconnects with session-scoped idempotency and multi-call interleaving.
- Load test: perf-canary scenario with a 30% capacity reduction validated that fail-fast reduces tail latency for high-priority routes while increasing 409+advice events (expected).
- Manual: exercised in staging against a small dedicated cluster and used the SDK to assert parsed retry advice fields.

Follow-ups and known limitations:
- TS/Go SDKs: follow-up PRs to provide the same convenience wrappers in the next week.
- We intentionally keep the Retry-Advice header small; future work may provide a richer JSON body for internal customers if necessary.
- Edge case: idempotent session semantics for multi-hop tool calls (tool -> external system -> callback) will require additional review; deferred to ENG-4507.

Summary of changes (single continuous string):
Adds Retry-Advice header + streaming control frame; introduces opt-in fail-fast request flag and server backpressure path; clarifies idempotency scoping for session vs call keys; normalizes short error code header for deterministic adapter mapping; implements Python SDK hooks and tests; adds rollout/feature-flagging and observability metrics.

review_comments: Ethan Miller: Important improvement. Two asks: 1) add a short canonical example line for client parsers in docs/api/retry_advice.md, 2) ensure the header parser defers to a fastpath when header absent.
Marina Lopez: responded - added compact example and non-alloc fastpath; included benchmark in control_test.go that shows <1% overhead in hot path.
Priya Shah: question on idempotency - how do we expect external tool webhooks to treat session-scoped keys? Suggest adding a sentence to idempotency-scoping.md.
Marina Lopez: replied - added guidance: webhooks should validate the call_id and avoid re-applying side-effects for session-scoped retries unless tool explicitly declares idempotent behavior.
Leo Tan: CI flaked once on the perf-canary. Re-ran - green now. Approving with small docs nits addressed.
Vikram Rao (SRE): suggest emitting a metric advice_rate_per_route to help tune fail-fast thresholds — added in this PR.
notes_for_release: Feature gated behind feature.retry_advice_v1. When enabled, clients may receive Retry-Advice and should prefer the small header over heuristics. SDKs provide helpers in Python; TS/Go follow-ups planned. Operators: use metrics advice_emitted and advice_consumed to monitor rollout impact.
operational_impact: Adds a small metric and feature flag; operators should monitor advice_emitted and increased 409 rates during staged rollout.
